Executive Summary

Wald Foodss Foods Facility in Burlington, IA is a pizza crust processing facility. Ammonia is used at our facility as the cooling medium in our refrigeration system. The ammonia is contained in a closed loop system; it is designed to remain inside the piping and vessels in our facility.  We believe that ammonia provides the safest and most efficient cooling choice for our operation. We have a strong commitment to operate our facility in a safe and responsible manner.

The ammonia refrigeration system is operated as a two stage system. On the low stage portion of the system, a low temperature accumulator operating at 40°F pumps liquid to a spiral freezer unit. The freezer unit is designed to freeze pizza crust. The low temperature ammonia liquid flows through the spiral freezer coils where it picks up heat, changing the ammonia from a liquid to a vapor. The low pressure ammonia vapor and any un-vaporized liquid is returned from the spiral freezer coils to the low temperature accumulator via a suction header.

Vapor from the low temperature accumulator is fed to a low stage compressor. The compressed vapor from the low stage compressor is sent to the high temperature accumulator operating at 20°F.

There are seven units in the Toppings area, three in the Packaging area and one makeup air handling unit which are connected to the high stage portion of the refrigeration system. The Toppings and Packaging coolers are designed to maintain a 40°F room temperature. The oven air handling unit is designed to supply cool air to maintain 100°F or less in the oven area. Pumps from the high temperature accumulator feed liquid to the evaporators and the air handling unit where it picks up heat, changing the ammonia from a liquid to a vapor. The ammonia vapor is sent from the evaporators and the air handling unit to the high temperature accumulator via a common suction header.

Vapor from the high temperature accumulator is fed to the high stage compressors. Dur

ing the compression phase in the high stage compressors, the temperature of the ammonia vapor will rise as the pressure of the ammonia vapor is increased to approximately 150  190 psig. The high pressure ammonia vapor flows from the high stage compressors to the evaporative condensers where heat is removed, turning the vapor into a high pressure liquid. The high pressure liquid is collected in a high pressure receiver.

The liquid collected in the high pressure receiver is fed to the compressor cooling lines and makeup for the low and high temperature accumulators.

The emergency action plan at Wald Family Foods requires all associates to be trained in safe evacuation and notification procedures in cases of actual or drill emergencies. Training shall include escape routes, notification of appropriate response agencies, instructions on activating a building fire alarm system and what should be done after evacuating a building. The evacuation alarm and emergency evacuation procedures will be tested no less than once per year. The decision of when to practice evacuating the building will rest with the Plant Manager. Arrangements have been made to coordinate Wald Family Foods Emergency Action Plan and applicable emergency services with the following local agencies:

       Incident Discovery
All employees discovering an ammonia odor shall alert the nearest supervisor immediately of the situation and move to a safe location. The supervisor shall immediately notify Maintenance to investigate the issue. The Refrigeration Technician will investigate the ammonia odor following Incident Investigation Procedures.  The Refrigeration Technician will assess the situation by taking air samples with a calibrated portable ammonia detector to determine the concentration, if any, of ammonia and determine if employees need to evacuate the area.

Any smell or release of ammonia shall be documented and reported to the Senior PSM Specialist. Even small non reportable releases.

      Emergency Response Initiation 

      Handling Small incidental releases of Ammonia 
Upon discovery of the source of the ammonia release the technician can apply corrective measures to mitigate and isolate the release. These measures will vary according to the location and severity of the release. In some cases, very small releases may be stopped by direct action on the leaking component. 

Other releases of ammonia that cannot be stopped by direct action, or create an area that cannot be immediately entered, should be stopped by operational methods such as closing valves and/or turning off equipment. When it is impossible to sufficiently isolate and stop a small release, then Handling Large Emergency Releases procedure shall be followed. 

     Handling Large Emergency Releases of Ammonia 
Refrigeration Technician shall contact an Incident Commander or the onsite maintenance supervisor to inform them of the situation. If an Incident Commander is not readily available, the maintenance supervisor will be the acting Incident Commander until relieved by an official facility Incident Commander.

If the emergency is life threatening the Incident Commander shall call 911 and then contact site leadership to make them aware 911 has been called.

When reporting an ammonia release to the 911 operator the following information must be provided:
	State that there is an ammonia release.
	Give physical address of Wald Family Foods (3400 Mt. Pleasant St., Burlington, IA 52601)
	Give specific location within the building of the release, if known
	Description of any injuries
	Stay on the line until told to hang up.

The Incident Commander or their designee shall contact the following to inform them of the Emergency Release:
	Director of Safety and Loss Prevention
	Presid

ent of Wald Family Foods
	Plant Manager

In response to an ammonia release, Wald Family Foods will not respond to releases of hazardous chemicals in an offensive manner. The facility does not have any employees trained at the HAZMAT Technicians or First Responders Operations Level.  However, in the case of a minor ammonia release, designated maintenance personnel are allowed to isolate or maintain the release.

Wald Family Foods has not had any accidental releases reported since the commissioning of the plant.

The worst case release scenario would be failure of the high temperature accumulator releasing 7,610 lbs. of ammonia (the entire charge) for duration of ten minutes. Under worst-case weather conditions, ammonia could travel 0.6 miles before dispersing enough to no longer pose a hazard to the public.  This scenario is unlikely for the following reasons:	
- Worst case weather conditions are uncommon,
- Industry standards for the manufacture and quality control of pressure vessels
- Ammonia is not corrosive in this service
- Pressure safety valves limit operating pressure in this vessel
- The accident prevention program in place at the facility including the mechanical integrity program for regular maintenance, inspection and testing and replacement of equipment, if necessary
- Installed ammonia sensors in the system to warn of leaks
- Alarms in place to warn operating personnel of process upsets
- The emergency action plan and equipment in place at the facility

The alternative case release scenario involves an outdoor release of gas through a ½ hole in a pipe containing ammonia under a pressure of 180 psig.  For the release of gas, we found the distance to the endpoint to be 0.2 miles.  The scenario of an alternative case ammonia release is unlikely due to the following reasons:

1. The mechanical integrity program for regular maintenance, inspection and testing, and replacement of equipment if necessary.
2. The emergency action plan at the facility.
